title: Structured Outputs & Tool Interfaces
description: Study design a minimal schema, validate and repair deterministically, describe tool parameters precisely, and handle tool results as evidence. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Design a minimal schema
lessons.description: Define separate schema validation and source-value verification.
lessons.conceptOverview: A schema defines fields, types and allowed values. Keep it aligned with downstream needs and use explicit missing-value rules; structural constraints do not guarantee factual correctness.
lessons.whyItMatters: Structure and factual support require separate validation.

lessons.title: Validate and repair deterministically
lessons.description: Specify semantic validation and a bounded failure response.
lessons.conceptOverview: Parse outputs and enforce required fields, ranges and enumerations in application code. If repair is attempted, bound retries and retain the original failure rather than silently accepting malformed results.
lessons.whyItMatters: Parsing success does not replace semantic validation.

lessons.title: Describe tool parameters precisely
lessons.description: Add a timezone requirement and runtime rejection of ambiguous input.
lessons.conceptOverview: Tool descriptions should explain required inputs, units and valid usage. Authorization and business checks remain in the application; a clear description cannot grant permission to act.
lessons.whyItMatters: Tool inputs need precise semantics and runtime checks.

lessons.title: Handle tool results as evidence
lessons.description: Specify an empty-result response and a success-evidence condition.
lessons.conceptOverview: Returned tool data may be incomplete, stale or untrusted. Ask for answers grounded in the actual result and define behavior for errors instead of fabricating a successful outcome.
lessons.whyItMatters: A claimed action or fact should be supported by the tool result.
